title: Paired drawers: Positive proof strip
topics: Two pointers, windows and prefix sums
summary: The input contains exactly two sorted drawers. Produce all their readings in one sorted sequence, preserving duplicates. Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.
descriptionMd:
Two sorted dispatch trays must feed one shared label printer without losing repeated tags. Sol prepares a clean proof strip for the front desk. Positive derived readings keep their places relative to one another.

The input contains exactly two sorted drawers. Produce all their readings in one sorted sequence, preserving duplicates.

Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates.

Implement pairedDrawersPositiveProofStrip(drawers, k). k is part of the common inspection-card signature and does not affect this task's result.
unitIntro: Two sorted streams. The input contains exactly two sorted drawers. Produce all their readings in one sorted sequence, preserving duplicates. Keep the sequence order specified here before computing the requested receipt. A scan invariant says what has been processed and what remains. Work through the proof strip first, then change the returned summary without changing the definition of that sequence. The last card revisits loop accumulators from Hello, Keys.
constraints: 1 <= k <= 8. All arithmetic results fit a signed 32-bit integer.
Numeric readings lie between -1,000,000 and 1,000,000, subject to the task's shape and ordering rules.
The input has exactly two rows, each containing at most 64 integers.

Target time O(n); auxiliary space including the derived sequence O(n). n is the input length; d distinct values; q query count; M maximum reading; V vertices; E edges; h tree height; r reported tree nodes.
hints: Start with two sorted streams. What state describes the portion you have already processed?

The input contains exactly two sorted drawers. Produce all their readings in one sorted sequence, preserving duplicates. Derive each required reading once; do not restart the whole procedure for every output position.
Return only the strictly positive values in the derived sequence, preserving their relative order and duplicates. Handle the empty derived sequence according to the stated return rule.
